source: Yes, yes. I anticipate he and his little cretinous attaché are somewhere in the marshes near this castle at the moment.
But if we both know that, surely we can stop it.
Oh? Can we, now?
...And you know how I can achieve this.
Now leave me. Giving you a hint at this stage would be cheating, dearheart.
Not while the men in charge of allocating this castle's defenses are unconvinced of any wrongdoing.
If only there were someone who knew Fortinbras closely who might be willing to come forward.
Bernardo, I have proof of Fortinbras's plan to betray Denmark. He's hiding out in Castle Town.
You... Ophelia. My deepest pardons. Could you repeat that? I thought you said...
You heard correctly. Fortinbras is hiding out in Castle Town as we speak.
He and his officers are in disguise near the tavern, in a small apartment.
If we act immediately and send men to arrest them, we may be able to stop their coup in its tracks.
I believe you. That look in your eye. It frightens me to no end.
Regretfully, I am unable to perform such an action without the King and Polonius's explicit consent.
As his advisor, your father must be consulted in situations like these. I'll call a War Council immediately.
If possible, I request that you allow your father and me to break this news to the King. He may not trust your word on this matter.
I want to be present at that meeting.
That's impossible. My apologies, my lady.
Upon second thought, it's only impossible if the King knows of your presence.
So you'll allow me to observe in secret?
You're certainly small enough to hide nicely.
One of the rare benefits.
Come to the King's room when the meeting convenes. We'll speak further then.
Regretfully, I am unable to perform such an action without the King's explicit consent.
I'll call a War Council immediately.
If possible, I request that you allow me to break this news to the King. He may not trust your word on this matter.
According to law, I'm unable to perform such an action without the King's explicit consent.
It could be perceived as an act of war, depending on the outcome.
Once the dust has settled, I'll gather the nobility and ask them to recommend an action.
But Bernardo, we don't have time like that. Fortinbras could march on us today.
I cannot act alone on a whim, Ophelia.
The King is dead. There are bigger matters at play right now.
Father, I have proof of Fortinbras's plan to betray Denmark. He's hiding out in Castle Town.
Remember when we spoke earlier and you mentioned needing proof? I have it in hand.
This is the proof I know you've been searching for, Father.
We must seize this fast, or we will all be conquered. The war is coming to our front.
Please believe me!
I believe it.
But I must also verify it.
Then send soldiers into town. He and his officers are hiding in disguise near the tavern, in a small apartment.
Hrm. Alas, I don't have the authority to propose such a move alone. I must consult with Bernardo and His Majesty.
Luckily, such a meeting can easily be arranged.
Luckily, such a meeting has already been arranged. Perhaps due to your intervention?
The War Council will congregate as soon as we are able, in the King's personal chambers.
Am I... may I be permitted to witness it?
...Under ordinary circumstances, absolutely not. No women are permitted to attend to matters of war.
And the King must not know this tip came from you, else he'll be unlikely to believe it.
...However, given that you seem to have been particularly interested in this matter lately...
Perhaps there's a way. Join us outside the King's quarters, and I'll see what we might do.
But with Claudius's death, we've entered a period of ambiguity.
No one in the castle has the authority to bring men down upon Fortinbras. It would essentially be an act of war.
If he's trying to come to our gates, isn't an act of war exactly what we need?
It's more complicated than that.
Regardless, I expect the nobility will come together to vote upon a successor in just a few days. At that time, we'll speak further of pursuing Fortinbras.
(We don't have days. Just hours. But he'd never believe that.)
Your Highness, I know for certain that Prince Fortinbras is hiding out in Castle Town as we speak.
Charming. Are we playing at something?
No. This is quite serious. I know it seems sudden, but I also think you might be the one to believe me.
I've seen them with my own eyes. They're in disguise, hiding out near the inn in a small apartment.
Oh, dear. You are serious.
Why don't you speak about these things with Guard Captain Bernardo? I'm sure Bernardo can allay your concerns.
Even if I did believe you, I have no authority to act in these sorts of scenarios. Ansy matter of war rests between my husband, his chief advisor, and his military advisor.
His chief advisor was your father. But perhaps Bernardo can still assist.
I think either of those latter two could lend you an ear for a moment. I imagine it might help to put your mind at ease.
Prince Fortinbras is here, in town, hiding out with some of his men. I know you know this, too.
Are you insane?
I know about all of it. Your father pressured you into this. You didn't want to help him. To help Fortinbras. But you weren't given a choice.
You're going to continue meeting with him until he has all the information he needs to overtake Elsinore. And then, Brit-- then everyone will die.
And you don't want that any more than I do. Because despite your tough external demeanor, you actually like some of the people in this castle, don't you?
Witch. You're a witch. That's the only possible explanation. A nosy, no-good witch.
But, fine. You called my bluff. And you're right about all of it, of course. So what now, witch?
This meeting you're going to attend with him? It's not going to end the way you think it will. And when the dust settles, Brit, everyone here will die.
Soon, Brit, everyone here will die.
What, then? What exactly are the two of us supposed to do?
I know that if we work together, we can find a way out of this.
We need to make sure Fortinbras is brought safely into Elsinore's custody.
Hah! Any idiot with a little political clout can do that. Try Bernardo, for one. But arresting him won't be the hard part, you know.
Let's say Fortinbras is dragged back to Elsinore in chains and thrown into the dungeon. He's got eyes and ears all over the castle.
Those eyes will watch for any opportune moment-- and then they'll find him and release him back to his men.
Any good chess player knows that check is the easy part. But the king can flee. It's checkmate you need to be worried about. Once you have this 'king', how will you keep him?
Look, Ophelia-- a little free advice between friends...
You need to control the chaos afterwards. Ensure that nothing goes wrong so that all attention can be focused on keeping ol' Norway Junior under lock and key.
That's the part neither of us are in a position to control, though. Unless you know something I don't.
(I know a few things, in fact.)
My King, I have proof of Fortinbras's plan to betray Denmark. He's hiding out in Castle Town.
Wah hah hah. Do tell, Ophelia. What have you dreamed up now?
It wasn't a dream. It was real. I saw him and some of his officers. They're all hiding out near the inn, in a small apartment.
Silence. I tire of this.
Go trouble someone else with these assertions.
(He won't even give it a second thought...)
(But someone else might.)
Are you being quite serious?
I wouldn't tell you if I didn't think you'd believe me.
Look into my eyes. Do you think I'd deceive you?
Well, love, if it'll put your mind at ease, I'll call a small council.
We can at least investigate the matter, I suppose. It's trivial to do so.
My father has, in his possession, some notes written by King Hamlet before his death.
Do you know how I might be able to read them?
Notes written by my brother...?
Thank you for alerting me to this, Ophelia. No doubt this is a matter your father and I ought to have settled.
If they are possessions of my brother's, they belong with me, to be certain.
Your forthcoming attitude towards this matter is admirable, especially among your own kin.
Sadly, your father's passing has made reconciling this affair rather more difficult.
I cannot interrogate those who are no longer with us.
My father has, in his possession, some notes written by King Hamlet before his death. What do you know of them?
Notes... written by... my husband Hamlet?
Yes, my lady.
Why... wouldn't he have given them to me? How could Polonius have something like that?
After my husband's passing, your father was ordered to hand over all such documents to myself and Claudius.
What could they contain?
They must have been stolen. Confidential information withheld from me. Against my direct orders, no less.
And now he's gone. And I cannot even confront him about it.
I've wondered so many times whether my husband might have left any last words for me.
Now I'll never know.
Ahh... There's no proof of that yet, my lady.
No. That's the only reason I wouldn't know about these notes, if they exist.
I'll have his rooms searched immediately.
King Hamlet evidently wrote some notes before his death, which my father now has hidden. What do you know of them?
It's true. Your father's spirit told me as much.
My... father's spirit spoke to you, too? Then I believe it.
Thankfully, now that Claudius is dead, my father can be at peace.
I'd like to follow up on his personal writings—next week, perhaps, if I find time.
Perhaps they contain some uncharted wisdom on his own rule.
There would be no reason to keep those private, if they existed. Unless...
Ophelia... do you think your father might be trying to hide something from me? Something about my father's... death?
It's possible. But Hamlet, please don't be rash...
I think I'd better go see the dear old fool.
But your father is dead. And of course, all this is to blame for it.
Just one more secret a man took to his grave.
